rejected.reason: Devīgītā 8.46 is a festival calendar verse (śrāvaṇa month); the Rāvaṇa stem there is a false match (likely in a compound or incidental mention). No Purāṇic account of Rāvaṇa's backstory available in corpus. Reject.

Sundara V.23.6-7 gives Rāvaṇa's Purāṇic genealogy (Brahmā → Pulastya → Viśravā → Rāvaṇa). This IS a genuine Purāṇic anchor passage — but it requires the Viṣṇupurāṇa or Brahma-Purāṇa, not the Devīgītā. Devīgītā 3.30 mentions prajāpati as a body part in viśvarūpa — completely unrelated to Rāvaṇa's lineage. Reject due to source mismatch; the note concept is valid but must await VishṇuP corpus addition.

Devīgītā Brahmā appearances are in Śākta theological lists (Brahmā as subordinate to Devī). Sundara uses brahmā in standard epic theogony (brahmāstra, svayambhū). The Śākta register adds nothing to Sundara commentary. Reject.
kalpa in Sundara = 'resembling' (kalpate), not 'cosmic cycle'. Devīgītā kalpa = kalpavṛkṣa (wish-tree) or 'determined'. Semantic mismatch. Reject.
Śrī in Sundara is a common honorific/auspiciousness marker (śrīmān, śrīmatī). Devīgītā śrī contexts are Śākta theology. No specific verse-level parallel. Reject.
Lakṣmī in Sundara = beauty/prosperity simile. Devīgītā 8.5 = sacred geography (Kolāpura). Thematic overlap too generic. Reject.
Meru in Devīgītā 5.29 = yoga anatomy (merudaṇḍa = spine). Sundara meru = mountain simile. Semantic mismatch (anatomy vs. geography). Reject.

Sundara V.48.15 dakṣasuta = sons of Dakṣa = gods (standard epithet). Devīgītā 1.47 mentions dakṣaduhitara (Dakṣa's daughter = Satī). Unrelated: one is Rāvaṇa's son fighting gods, the other is Devī's birth. Reject.

Devīgītā Vāyu = cosmic element (air) in Sāṃkhya or yoga context (one of five elements, prāṇa-movement). Sundara Vāyu = Hanumān's divine father. The cosmological element connection is too remote from the narrative genealogy. Reject.
